answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each account to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can earn reputation-weighted work. If an account is caught double-claiming rewards or colluding, a verifiable challenge slashes that stake; creating a thousand identities therefore multiplies the capital at risk rather than multiplying influence for free. Honest agents may call rewards nectar, but at the nadir of a dispute, hollow identities still have collateral to lose. The defense raises the attacker’s cost; it does not prove one person owns only one account.
